102: E.g., `old(a + b + c) == old(a) + old(b) + old(c)` and `old(old(g)) == old(g)`.
103: -/
104: def normalizeOldExpr (e : Expression.Expr) (inOld : Bool := false)
105:   : Expression.Expr :=
106:   match _He : e with
107:   | .fvar _ v ty =>
108:     if inOld then
109:       @oldVar e.metadata e.metadata e.metadata none v ty -- ignoring the operation type
110:     else e
111:   | .const _ _ | .bvar _ _ | .op _ _ _ => e
112:   | .abs m ty e' => .abs m ty (normalizeOldExpr e' inOld)
113:   | .quant m qk ty tr' e' => .quant m qk ty (normalizeOldExpr tr' inOld) (normalizeOldExpr e' inOld)
114:   | .app m e1 e2 =>
115:     match _He1 : e1 with
116:     | .op m o ty =>
117:       if _Hop : o = "old" then
118:         -- is an old var or old expr
119:         match _He2 : e2 with
120:         | .fvar _ _ _ => e
121:         | e' => normalizeOldExpr e' true
122:       else
123:         .app m (normalizeOldExpr e1 inOld) (normalizeOldExpr e2 inOld)
124:     | _ => .app m (normalizeOldExpr e1 inOld) (normalizeOldExpr e2 inOld)
125:   | .ite m c t f => .ite m (normalizeOldExpr c inOld)
126:                       (normalizeOldExpr t inOld) (normalizeOldExpr f inOld)
127:   | .eq m e1 e2 => .eq m (normalizeOldExpr e1 inOld) (normalizeOldExpr e2 inOld)
128:     termination_by sizeOf e
129:   decreasing_by
130:     all_goals simp [sizeOf, Lambda.LExpr.sizeOf]; try simp_all; omega
131: 
132: def normalizeOldExprs (sm : List Expression.Expr) :=
133:   sm.map normalizeOldExpr
134: 
135: def normalizeOldCheck (c : Procedure.Check) : Procedure.Check :=
136:   { c with expr := normalizeOldExpr c.expr }
137: 
138: def normalizeOldChecks (c : ListMap String Procedure.Check) : ListMap String Procedure.Check :=
139:   c.map (λ p ↦ (p.fst, normalizeOldCheck p.snd))
140: 
141: /--
142: Checks if `e` contains an application of the `old` function.
143: 
144: This function is agnostic of old expression normalization (see
145: `normalizeOldExpr`). Also see `extractOldExprVars` that extracts `var` from
146: `old(var)` after normalization.
147: -/
148: def containsOldExpr (e : Expression.Expr) : Bool :=
149:   match e with
150:   | .op _ (CoreIdent.unres "old") _ => true
151:   | .op _ _ _ => false
152:   | .const _ _ | .bvar _ _ | .fvar _ _ _ => false
153:   | .abs _ _ e' => containsOldExpr e'
154:   | .quant _ _ _ tr' e' => containsOldExpr tr' || containsOldExpr e'
155:   | .app _ e1 e2 => containsOldExpr e1 || containsOldExpr e2
156:   | .ite _ c t f => containsOldExpr c || containsOldExpr t || containsOldExpr f
157:   | .eq _ e1 e2 => containsOldExpr e1 || containsOldExpr e2
158: 
159: /--
160: Get a list of original global variable names that are referred to in an
161: `old(...)` expression. Note that `expr` below should be normalized by
162: `normalizeOldExpr`.
163: -/
164: def extractOldExprVars (expr : Expression.Expr)
165:   : List Expression.Ident := match expr with
166:   | .const _ _ | .bvar _ _ | .fvar _ _ _ | .op _ _ _ => []
167:   | .abs _ _ e => extractOldExprVars e
168:   | .quant _ _ _ tr e => extractOldExprVars tr ++ extractOldExprVars e
169:   | .app _ e1 e2 => match e1, e2 with
170:     | .op _ (CoreIdent.unres "old") _, .fvar _ v _ => [v]
171:     | .op _ (CoreIdent.unres "old") _, _ => panic! s!"Old expression {expr} not normalized"
172:     | e1', e2' => extractOldExprVars e1' ++ extractOldExprVars e2'
173:   | .ite _ c t e => extractOldExprVars c ++ extractOldExprVars t ++ extractOldExprVars e
174:   | .eq _ e1 e2 => extractOldExprVars e1 ++ extractOldExprVars e2
175: 
176: /--
177: Substitute `old(var)` in expression `e` with `s`.
178: -/
179: def substOld (var : Expression.Ident) (s e : Expression.Expr) :
180:   Expression.Expr :=
181:   match e with
182:   | .const _ _ | .fvar _ _ _ | .bvar _ _ | .op _ _ _ => e
183:   | .abs m ty e' => .abs m ty (substOld var s e')
184:   | .quant m qk ty tr' e' => .quant m qk ty (substOld var s tr') (substOld var s e')
185:   | .app m e1 e2 =>
186:     match e1, e2 with
187:     | .op _ (CoreIdent.unres "old") _, .fvar _ x _ =>
188:       -- NOTE: We rely on the typeChecker to normalize `e` ensure that `old` is
189:       -- only used with an `fvar`.
190:       if x == var
191:         -- substitute, if should be substituted
192:         then s
193:         else e
194:     | _, _ => .app m (substOld var s e1) (substOld var s e2)
195:   | .ite m c t f => .ite m (substOld var s c)
196:                       (substOld var s t) (substOld var s f)
197:   | .eq m e1 e2 => .eq m (substOld var s e1) (substOld var s e2)
198: 
199: /--
200: For each `(var, val)` in `sm`, substitute `old(var)` in expression `e` with
201: `val`.
202: -/
203: def substsOldExpr (sm : Map Expression.Ident Expression.Expr) (e : Expression.Expr)
204:   : Expression.Expr :=
205:   if sm.isEmpty then e else
206:   match e with
207:   | .const _ _ | .fvar _ _ _ | .bvar _ _ | .op _ _ _ => e
208:   | .abs m ty e' => .abs m ty (substsOldExpr sm e')
209:   | .quant m qk ty tr' e' => .quant m qk ty (substsOldExpr sm tr') (substsOldExpr sm e')
210:   | .app m e1 e2 =>
211:     match e1, e2 with
212:     | .op _ (CoreIdent.unres "old") _, .fvar _ x _ =>
213:       match sm.find? x with
214:       | some s => s
215:       | none => e
216:     | _, _ => .app m (substsOldExpr sm e1) (substsOldExpr sm e2)
217:   | .ite m c t f => .ite m (substsOldExpr sm c)
218:                       (substsOldExpr sm t) (substsOldExpr sm f)
219:   | .eq m e1 e2 => .eq m (substsOldExpr sm e1) (substsOldExpr sm e2)
220: 
221: /--
222: For each `(var, val)` in `sm`, substitute `old(var)` in each expression `es`
223: with `val`.
224: -/
225: def substsOldExprs (sm : Map Expression.Ident Expression.Expr) (es : List Expression.Expr) :=
226:   es.map $ substsOldExpr sm
227: 
228: theorem substsOldExpr_singleton: substsOldExpr [(var,s)] e = substOld var s e := by
229:   induction e <;> simp [substsOldExpr, substOld, Map.isEmpty, *]
230:   split <;> simp_all;
231:   simp [Map.find?]
232:   split <;> simp_all
233:   intro h; rw [Eq.comm] at h
234:   contradiction
235: 
236: theorem substOldExpr_nil: OldExpressions.substsOldExpr [] e = e := by
237:   unfold OldExpressions.substsOldExpr
238:   simp [Map.isEmpty]
239: 
240: /--
241: For each `(var, expr)` pair in `sm`, substitute `old(var)` with `expr` in
242: `conds`.
243: -/
244: protected def substsOldInProcChecks {Ty}

open Lean.Meta.SolveByElim (SolveByElimConfig mkAssumptionSet)

/--
Allow elaboration of `Config` arguments to tactics.
-/
declare_config_elab elabConfig Lean.Meta.SolveByElim.SolveByElimConfig

/--
Allow elaboration of `ApplyRulesConfig` arguments to tactics.
-/
declare_config_elab elabApplyRulesConfig Lean.Meta.SolveByElim.ApplyRulesConfig

/--
Parse the lemma argument of a call to `solve_by_elim`.
The first component should be true if `*` appears at least once.
The second component should contain each term `t`in the arguments.
The third component should contain `t` for each `-t` in the arguments.
-/
def parseArgs (s : Option (TSyntax ``args)) :
    Bool × List Term × List Term :=
  let args : Array (TSyntax ``arg) := match s with
  | some s => match s with
    | `(args| [$args,*]) => args.getElems
    | _ => #[]
  | none => #[]
  let args : Array (Option (Term ⊕ Term)) := args.map fun t => match t with
    | `(arg| $_:star) => none
    | `(arg| - $t:term) => some (Sum.inr t)
    | `(arg| $t:term) => some (Sum.inl t)
    | _ => panic! "Unreachable parse of solve_by_elim arguments."
  let args := args.toList
  (args.contains none,
    args.filterMap fun o => o.bind Sum.getLeft?,
    args.filterMap fun o => o.bind Sum.getRight?)

/-- Parse the `using ...` argument for `solve_by_elim`. -/
def parseUsing (s : Option (TSyntax ``using_)) : Array Ident :=
  match s with
  | some s => match s with
    | `(using_ | using $ids,*) => ids.getElems
    | _ => #[]
  | none => #[]

/-- Wrapper for `solveByElim` that processes a list of `Term`s
that specify the lemmas to use. -/
def processSyntax (cfg : SolveByElimConfig := {}) (only star : Bool) (add remove : List Term)
    (use : Array Ident) (goals : List MVarId) : MetaM (List MVarId) := do
  if !remove.isEmpty && goals.length > 1 then
    throwError "Removing local hypotheses is not supported when operating on multiple goals."
  let ⟨lemmas, ctx⟩ ← mkAssumptionSet only star add remove use
  SolveByElim.solveByElim cfg lemmas ctx goals

@[builtin_tactic Lean.Parser.Tactic.applyAssumption]
def evalApplyAssumption : Tactic := fun stx =>
  match stx with
  | `(tactic| apply_assumption $cfg:optConfig $[only%$o]? $[$t:args]? $[$use:using_]?) => do
    let (star, add, remove) := parseArgs t
    let use := parseUsing use
    let cfg ← elabConfig (mkOptionalNode cfg)
    let cfg := { cfg with
      backtracking := false
      maxDepth := 1 }
    replaceMainGoal (← processSyntax cfg o.isSome star add remove use [← getMainGoal])
  | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax

/--
Elaborator for apply_rules.

See `Lean.MVarId.applyRules` for a `MetaM` level analogue of this tactic.
-/
@[builtin_tactic Lean.Parser.Tactic.applyRules]
def evalApplyRules : Tactic := fun stx =>
  match stx with
  | `(tactic| apply_rules $cfg:optConfig $[only%$o]? $[$t:args]? $[$use:using_]?) => do
    let (star, add, remove) := parseArgs t
    let use := parseUsing use
    let cfg ← elabApplyRulesConfig (mkOptionalNode cfg)
    let cfg := { cfg with backtracking := false }
    liftMetaTactic fun g => processSyntax cfg o.isSome star add remove use [g]
  | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax

@[builtin_tactic Lean.Parser.Tactic.solveByElim]
def evalSolveByElim : Tactic
  | `(tactic| solve_by_elim $[*%$s]? $cfg:optConfig $[only%$o]? $[$t:args]? $[$use:using_]?) => do
    let (star, add, remove) := parseArgs t
    let use := parseUsing use
    let goals ← if s.isSome then
      getGoals
    else
      pure [← getMainGoal]
    let cfg ← elabConfig cfg
    let [] ← processSyntax cfg o.isSome star add remove use goals |
      throwError "Internal error: `solve_by_elim` unexpectedly returned subgoals"
    pure ()
  | _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax

instance [DecidableEq α] : DecidableRel (Subset : List α → List α → Prop) :=
  fun _ _ => decidableBAll _ _

/-! ### Sublist and isSublist -/

/--
The first list is a non-contiguous sub-list of the second list. Typically written with the `<+`
operator.

In other words, `l₁ <+ l₂` means that `l₁` can be transformed into `l₂` by repeatedly inserting new
elements.
-/
inductive Sublist {α} : List α → List α → Prop
  /-- The base case: `[]` is a sublist of `[]` -/
  | slnil : Sublist [] []
  /-- If `l₁` is a subsequence of `l₂`, then it is also a subsequence of `a :: l₂`. -/
  | cons a : Sublist l₁ l₂ → Sublist l₁ (a :: l₂)
  /-- If `l₁` is a subsequence of `l₂`, then `a :: l₁` is a subsequence of `a :: l₂`. -/
  | cons₂ a : Sublist l₁ l₂ → Sublist (a :: l₁) (a :: l₂)

@[inherit_doc] scoped infixl:50 " <+ " => Sublist

/--
True if the first list is a potentially non-contiguous sub-sequence of the second list, comparing
elements with the `==` operator.

The relation `List.Sublist` is a logical characterization of this property.

  simp [subset_def]

/-! ### Sublist and isSublist -/

@[simp, grind ←] theorem nil_sublist : ∀ l : List α, [] <+ l
  | [] => .slnil
  | a :: l => (nil_sublist l).cons a

@[simp, grind ←] theorem Sublist.refl : ∀ l : List α, l <+ l
  | [] => .slnil
  | a :: l => (Sublist.refl l).cons₂ a
